entries.name: Pi-model
entries.definition: A semi-supervised classifier-training procedure that combines labeled cross-entropy with squared disagreement between two stochastic predictions of the same input from a shared-parameter network, propagating gradients through both predictions.
entries.identity_notes: The Greek Π notation is an identity alias for the Pi-model in Laine and Aila, not the generic AIO Model class. Its two contemporaneous stochastic predictions and two-sided gradient differ from temporal ensembling’s stored predictions, Mean Teacher’s weight-averaged stopped-gradient teacher, and SimSiam’s asymmetric stopped-gradient representation targets. This record describes a training algorithm, not a trained checkpoint or fixed network architecture. The inspected AIO SemiSupervisedLLM class specifically combines LLM pretraining with supervised fine-tuning; its related synonym self-training is not an exact identity for this method. AIO SelfsupervisedLearning excludes human-annotated labels, Distillation describes large-to-small compression, and RegularizationLayer is a layer: none supplies an equivalent class for this algorithm. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 230 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in both worktree and main checkout; matches concern prior discovery leads and the Pi-model normalization regression. Ten exact AIO CLASS nodes, their scoped synonyms and outgoing edges, plus five neighboring native records were inspected. The corrected Unicode-aware normalizer preserves Π; the previous Pi-model/Model collision was a lexical defect, not semantic identity (review issue #58).

entries.name: Temporal ensembling
entries.definition: A semi-supervised classifier-training procedure that regularizes a current stochastic prediction toward a bias-corrected exponential average of earlier predictions for the same indexed training example, alongside labeled cross-entropy.
entries.identity_notes: This is the prediction-ensemble algorithm in Laine and Aila, distinguished from the same paper’s Pi-model. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in both worktree and main checkout; matches concern prior discovery leads and the Pi-model normalization regression. limitations: Per-example prediction memory scales with the number of indexed examples and classes; targets depend on preserving example identity across visits.

claims.statement: Maintain zero-initialized N-by-C arrays Z and target z_tilde for N indexed examples and C classes. During epoch t, obtain one stochastic prediction z_i for each example when its minibatch is processed. Minimize labeled cross-entropy divided by the full minibatch size plus w(t)/(C|B|) sum over all i in B of ||z_i−z_tilde_i||², holding the stored targets constant during differentiation. After predictions have been used for that epoch, update each accumulated prediction Z_i←alpha Z_i+(1−alpha)z_i and set the next target to Z_i/(1−alpha^t), with fixed 0≤alpha<1 and t starting at 1. Set the first epoch’s consistency weight to zero and ramp it up. Algorithm 2 displays the target update after the epoch; its caption permits per-example updates within a minibatch after the old target has been used. Predictions gathered within an epoch can come from different current parameter states. The exponential average is over example predictions, not model parameters.

claims.statement: Evaluate each input with independently perturbed student and teacher networks of the same architecture. Train the student with cross-entropy on labeled examples and a weighted squared-probability consistency cost between student and teacher predictions on labeled and unlabeled examples. Treat teacher predictions as constant during the gradient update. After obtaining the updated student parameters theta_t, update teacher parameters theta_prime_t←alpha theta_prime_(t−1)+(1−alpha)theta_t. Thus the teacher changes by parameter averaging after training steps, not by backpropagation through its consistency branch. Choose the averaging coefficient and consistency-weight schedule as part of the training setup. The core description does not require a particular initialization or warm-up formula. Unlike temporal ensembling, it does not require a persistent target array indexed by the training set.

entries.name: MixMatch
entries.definition: A semi-supervised classifier-training procedure that averages predictions over augmented unlabeled inputs, sharpens the resulting soft targets, mixes augmented labeled and unlabeled input-target pairs, and optimizes labeled cross-entropy plus an unlabeled squared-probability loss.
entries.identity_notes: MixMatch combines averaged augmented-view label guessing, probability sharpening and the modified MixUp pairing rule. These components define a distinct training algorithm rather than an alias for MixUp, Mean Teacher or a hard pseudo-label confidence filter. Its classification soft targets differ from representation matching in BYOL, DINO and SimSiam. This record describes a training algorithm, not a trained checkpoint or fixed network architecture. The inspected AIO SemiSupervisedLLM class specifically combines LLM pretraining with supervised fine-tuning; its related synonym self-training is not an exact identity for this method. AIO SelfsupervisedLearning excludes human-annotated labels, Distillation describes large-to-small compression, and RegularizationLayer is a layer: none supplies an equivalent class for this algorithm. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in both worktree and main checkout; matches concern prior discovery leads and the Pi-model normalization regression. limitations: The original setup pairs B labeled examples with B unlabeled examples and K augmentations per unlabeled input. Alternative batching or interpolation rules require an explicit variant scope.

For 0<T<1 sharpening concentrates probability. As a curator consequence of the formula, the T→0 limit is one-hot only with a unique maximum; tied maxima retain equal limiting mass. T>1 smooths rather than sharpens.
Correct label-preserving augmentation and useful interpolation are assumptions; guessed labels can be wrong and the algorithm has no defining hard confidence threshold.

The record does not assert published error rates or universal superiority. Reported T, K, alpha, lambda_u and evaluation-EMA settings are experimental choices, not fixed constants of every implementation.

claims.statement: Given B labeled examples with one-hot labels and B unlabeled examples, augment each labeled input once and each unlabeled input K times. Average the current classifier probabilities across the K views of each unlabeled input, then sharpen the average q_bar using q_c=q_bar_c^(1/T)/sum_j q_bar_j^(1/T), for T>0; treat these guessed labels as constants during differentiation. Create augmented labeled pairs X_hat of size B and unlabeled pairs U_hat of size KB, then shuffle their concatenation into W. Mix each X_hat pair with the corresponding first B pairs in W, and each U_hat pair with the corresponding remaining KB pairs. For each MixUp operation draw lambda from Beta(alpha,alpha), alpha>0, set lambda_prime=max(lambda,1−lambda), and combine both inputs and targets with weights lambda_prime and 1−lambda_prime, keeping at least half of the first pair. For the resulting X_prime and U_prime, minimize average soft-target cross-entropy over X_prime plus lambda_u/(C|U_prime|) times sum over U_prime of squared target/prediction differences, where C is the number of classes. The reported implementation ramps lambda_u linearly. Guessed labels use current-model predictions; the evaluation-only weight EMA in Section 4.1 is not a Mean Teacher target generator.

native_neighbors.name: Virtual adversarial training
native_neighbors.definition: A prediction-smoothing regularization procedure that trains a model to preserve its current output distribution under approximately worst-case small input perturbations, constructing those perturbations without using target labels.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: VAT denotes the Miyato et al. procedure described in the 2018 manuscript revision. The virtual target is the model’s current prediction. Label-free perturbation construction does not mean the complete supervised or semi-supervised training objective has no labels. VAT is a component of IMSAT but is not that information-maximization framework or a generative adversarial network. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 203 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Ignored-inclusive word-delimited searches of both full checkouts returned 52 worktree and 75 main-checkout lines: existing component discussions and discovery/review references, plus unrelated ignored dependency text in main. Short acronyms were compared in normalized identities. Four nearest maintained mechanisms and eleven exact AIO candidate nodes with direct parent edges were inspected.
limitations: The Hessian direction relies on a local quadratic approximation and finite-difference power iteration. One iteration does not solve the exact finite-radius maximization and provides no certified adversarial robustness.
The perturbation radius, norm, input representation and regularization weight affect which prediction changes are penalized. Semantic label preservation is not guaranteed for arbitrary perturbations.
A constant classifier can have zero consistency loss; VAT alone does not identify meaningful classes. The task loss or other learning signals remain material.

The author code uses epsilon-stabilized vector normalization, so its returned vector need not have exactly the ideal radius. Batch-normalization handling and finite arithmetic also belong to implementation scope.

claims.statement: For a fixed parameter snapshot theta_hat, approximately maximize D(p_theta_hat(y|x)||p_theta_hat(y|x+r)) over ||r||_2<=epsilon; the reported classifier implementation uses KL divergence. At r=0 the smooth KL objective has zero value and first derivative. Its local quadratic approximation gives a dominant-Hessian-eigenvector direction. Approximate that direction by initializing a random unit vector, taking the gradient with respect to r at a small displacement xi*d, normalizing it, and optionally repeating this power-iteration approximation. Scale the resulting direction by epsilon. For a model update, hold both the teacher prediction and the selected perturbation fixed while minimizing D(p_theta_hat(y|x)||p_theta(y|x+r_vadv)). Average this regularizer over available inputs to obtain R_VAT, and minimize supervised negative log likelihood plus alpha times R_VAT. The general formulation can use labeled and unlabeled inputs; the inspected semi-supervised driver applies its VAT branch to the unlabeled-input tensor. The pinned code defaults to one iteration, detaches the teacher and perturbation construction, and computes KL from softmax probabilities and stable log-softmax values. Its vatent branch separately adds conditional entropy minimization.

Generate two global crops and optional local crops from each image; the teacher sees the global crops and the student sees all crops. Average cross-entropy −sum_i P_t(v)_i log P_s(v′)_i over teacher global crops and student crops of the same image, excluding the identical view, and average over images in the minibatch. Stop gradients through P_t, update student parameters by the loss, and update teacher parameters by theta_t←lambda theta_t+(1−lambda)theta_s, with lambda in [0,1]. Update c by an exponential moving average with center momentum in [0,1) of the raw teacher outputs over all global views in the distributed batch for use on subsequent batches. Both branches share backbone and projection-head architecture; downstream features are taken from the backbone before the head.

native_neighbors.name: Information maximizing self-augmented training
native_neighbors.definition: A discrete representation-learning procedure that combines self-augmentation consistency with an information objective, using categorical outputs for clustering or a pairwise approximation for multi-bit hashing.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: IMSAT is the named Hu et al. procedure with explicitly different clustering and hashing configurations. It learns discrete output variables, unlike continuous embedding dependence estimators. Its information between input and output, plus consistency to a fixed current prediction, differs from IIC information between two assignment variables. This umbrella record does not equate the categorical, nonuniform-prior and hash objectives. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 199 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Ignored-inclusive word-delimited searches of both full checkouts found eight prior discovery/review references in each. Short acronyms were compared in normalized record identities; broad text searches used the full names and longer aliases. Nearest maintained mechanisms and seven exact AIO nodes with incident edges were inspected.
limitations: Hashing truncates the information expansion; pairwise penalties do not establish joint independence or exact information for the full bit vector. The ordered-pair convention affects its relative regularization strength.

The minibatch KL inequality is an expectation bound from convexity, not a bound for every batch or a guarantee that finite stochastic optimization satisfies the prior constraint. Penalty-method idealizations do not certify the trained nonconvex network.

Consistency depends on suitable transformations and perturbation radii. A transformation can preserve a nuisance factor or change desired semantics. Balanced marginal entropy can conflict with genuinely imbalanced classes.

The pinned clustering code uses a weighted marginal entropy default; it must not be silently described as exact unit-weight mutual information. Epsilon stabilization and approximate virtual perturbations further distinguish numerical loss from ideal formulas.

Some reported image experiments use features from an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet and hyperparameter selection uses labeled clustering accuracy. Unsupervised final training does not mean every source of representation or model-selection information is label-free. No model was run.

claims.statement: For a current network snapshot, hold the original-input output distribution fixed and minimize cross-entropy against the network prediction on a transformed input, summed over discrete output components and averaged over samples. Transformations include random perturbations or virtual adversarial perturbations approximately chosen to maximize local prediction change. For categorical clustering use R_SAT−lambda[H(Y)−H(Y|X)], with the marginal obtained by averaging conditional predictions. The nonuniform-prior variant instead minimizes R_SAT+lambda H(Y|X) subject to KL(p(Y)||q(Y))≤delta, implemented with an increasing positive-part penalty. For binary hashing the factorized conditional model uses the truncated information objective sum_d I(X;Y_d)−sum_(d≠e) I(Y_d;Y_e), with ordered distinct bit pairs. The pinned hash code enumerates unordered pairs and multiplies their mutual-information sum by two, confirming that convention. Its clustering code detaches the teacher and implements epsilon-stabilized KL consistency. Ideal KL and cross-entropy have the same parameter gradient for a fixed teacher; the code adds epsilon inside the logarithm and therefore only approximates that unstabilized identity. That code defaults to H(Y|X)−4H(Y), a weighted entropy variant rather than the unit-weight information expression.
